4 November 2026

Quantum fields, duality and boundary reconstruction

A quantum field theory describes what can be measured in a region of space and how those measurements combine. As two insertions meet, their singular products encode interactions and symmetries.

We ask whether these local products, together with boundary observables and a physical state, determine a theory in the region it bounds. The aim is a reversible algebraic description that preserves order, collisions and boundary actions.

Breakthroughs

  1. 1

    Coefficient duality

    Achieved Two associative descriptions are related by explicit inverse constructions that retain full current coefficients and their collision operations.

    Why it matters · Domain and hypotheses · Proved in · Read more
    Why it matters
    This establishes associative chiral Koszul duality for the full coefficient systems, the algebraic foundation for comparing local fields and boundary actions.
    Domain and hypotheses
    A smooth separated finite-type scheme of positive pure dimension over a characteristic-zero field. The augmented associative algebras have scalar empty coefficient on the ordered-word or ordered collision-atlas carrier. Full differential-module duals are retained as pro-perfect coefficients, with their transported tensor product and geometric functors. The inverse constructions preserve the specified collision maps.
    Proved in
    Chiral Quantum Groups and Holography, §§10.1 and 10.5 for the word and atlas constructions, §§80.2–80.4 for full coefficient transposition and the associative geometric dual, and §128.3 for ordered-atlas convolution in higher dimension.
    Read more
    Associative duality and full coefficient duality.
  2. 2

    Explicit dual fields

    Achieved For a specified family of deformed jet fields, the dual coefficients come from explicit field products, with both collision orders preserved.

    Why it matters · Domain and hypotheses · Proved in · Read more
    Why it matters
    This connects the coefficient theorem to translated fields, their singular products and their local vacua.
    Domain and hypotheses
    Over the complex numbers at every finite precision of the formal parameter ℏ\hbar, with compatible reductions. The nonzero charged jet algebra AA comes from a bounded nonpositive finite-dimensional generator complex over a finite-dimensional commutative coefficient algebra. Its positive-charge, charge- and weight-homogeneous relation ideal is preserved by the differential, translation and commuting jet derivations. The pair factor is w(u)∈1+ℏℂ[u,u−1][[ℏ]]w(u)\in1+\hbar\mathbb C[u,u^{-1}][[\hbar]], with separation uu. The dual field object is the meromorphic current core of 𝔰𝔩2⊗A\mathfrak{sl}_2\otimes A, with its polynomial core, scalar map, charge and jet actions marked. Its exchange uses the joint rational recipient, inverting the constituent discriminants, cross differences and their field-parameter translates. The comparison retains all normal derivatives, spectators and both local vacuum actions.
    Proved in
    Chiral Quantum Groups and Holography, §452.8, “Meromorphic current fields for charged jet quotients,” on the marked charged-jet domain just specified.

  3. 3

    Free boundary reconstruction

    Achieved For specified polynomial observables of a free interval theory, each completed boundary algebra is recovered from its junction action, compatibly with finite sewing.

    Why it matters · Domain and hypotheses · Proved in · Read more
    Why it matters
    This supplies an explicit holographic reconstruction example connecting bulk fields, two boundary actions and the operation of joining intervals.
    Domain and hypotheses
    The free cotangent theory on an interval times a complex disk, with target a complex line and scalar coupling one. Its polynomial observable domain is generated by the four projected junction fields, two exterior traces and two specified normal primitives, together with their Dolbeault descendants and finite tangential derivatives. The semiderived categories retain the rational and jointly locally nilpotent regular-mode actions. Completions have finite polynomial or exterior output in each regular-mode row. Finite sewing compares these observables with their uncut counterparts and includes the conjugate fields at each join.
    Proved in
    Chiral Quantum Groups and Holography, §32.12, “A native free junction and its interval sewings,” and §32.13, “A semiderived reverse action,” with the regular-mode conditions and row completions stated here.

  4. 4

    Affine symmetry

    Achieved Current symmetries can be combined and made to act consistently on the affine vacuum boundary at every value of the level.

    Why it matters · Domain and hypotheses · Proved in · Read more
    Why it matters
    The construction supplies a product and boundary action with coherent units and collision maps, including at the critical levels where a normalized Sugawara formula is unavailable.
    Domain and hypotheses
    A finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero, with any invariant symmetric level form. Decisive obstructions

  • Quantum non-formality

    Rules out The polynomial traceless absolute quantum algebra cannot be replaced, up to multiplicative quasi-isomorphism, by its cohomology algebra when the squared quantum parameter is nonzero.

    Why it matters · Domain and hypotheses · Proved in · Read more
    Why it matters
    Its invariant higher operation is information that a reconstruction based only on the ordinary cohomology product would lose.
    Domain and hypotheses
    The displayed three-coordinate BRST algebra over ℂ[ℏ]\mathbb C[\hbar], and every scalar change ℏ↦λ\hbar\mapsto\lambda into a commutative complex algebra with λ2≠0\lambda^2\ne0. The obstruction allows arbitrary cohomology markings and maps that need not preserve units. At λ=0\lambda=0 the algebra is formal; this detector does not decide a nonzero square-zero parameter.
    Proved in
    A-infinity Chiral Algebras and 3D Holomorphic–Topological QFT, §11.8, “An intrinsic absolute obstruction.”
    Read more
    Quantum higher products.

  • Scalar augmentation

    Rules out No unital algebra homomorphism sends the nonzero-level Heisenberg mode algebra to its scalar field.

    Why it matters · Domain and hypotheses · Proved in · Read more
    Why it matters
    A state evaluation cannot serve as an algebra augmentation; the field vacuum and the isolated empty coefficient have distinct roles.
    Domain and hypotheses
    A characteristic-zero coefficient field and nonzero level κ\kappa. The relation [J1,J−1]=κ1[J_1,J_{-1}]=\kappa1 would map to 0=κ0=\kappa in commuting scalars. A linear vacuum evaluation still exists.
    Proved in
    Chiral Quantum Groups and Holography, §18.2, “Koszul duality relative to the coefficients,” for the nonzero-level Heisenberg mode algebra.
    Read more
    A current and its vacuum.

  • The ordinary tensor coproduct

    Rules out The full polynomial shuffle algebras admit no unital multiplicative, charge-preserving ordinary tensor coproduct, linear over the coefficient ring and with charge-zero projection as two-sided counit.

    Why it matters · Domain and hypotheses · Proved in · Read more
    Why it matters
    A quantum-group reconstruction must retain the actual exchange rule and coefficient domain when splitting observables between two factors.
    Domain and hypotheses
    The polynomial shuffle carriers over ℚ[h1,h2]\mathbb Q[h_1,h_2], with h3=−h1−h2h_3=-h_1-h_2, a=∑i<jhihja=\sum_{i<j}h_ih_j, and b=h1h2h3b=h_1h_2h_3, for shuffle factors K0(v)=v2+a+b/vK_0(v)=v^2+a+b/v and K1(v)=v2K0(v)K_1(v)=v^2K_0(v). Their current relation has nonzero reduced-coproduct defect 2be0⊗e02b\,e_0\otimes e_0, where e0e_0 is the charge-one constant current. The positive rational construction retains its braided interchange and collision localization.
    Proved in
    Chiral Quantum Groups and Holography, §308.14, for the full polynomial carriers and ordinary tensor product just specified.

Open problems

General field duality

Which nonabelian field theories realize the full coefficient duality? A solution must construct the second field space and compare its product, exchange, translations, representations and local vacuum with the transposed collision operations. The marked charged-jet theorem supplies a comparison with its specified 𝔰𝔩2\mathfrak{sl}_2 current core, scalar pair factor and joint rational exchange domain.

Interacting reconstruction

Can the two-boundary reconstruction and finite sewing of the free example be extended to an interacting theory? The comparison must come from the coupled action, retain supported contact terms and quantum differentials, and identify the physical state that evaluates observables. Matching a central coefficient alone does not supply these maps.

Geometric and arithmetic field realizations

How do the constructed Hall, automorphic and fusion coefficients act on independently defined geometric fields? Their products must be compared with the actual coefficient complexes, orientations, traces and states. Arithmetic comparisons must also retain the fusion junctions, cups and caps, and the objects at intermediate periods.

Compatible higher operations

Which comparisons preserve all the structures at once? The affine translation and Jacobi homotopies, the constructed transverse multiplication, and the boundary action require an operation-compatible line comparison. More generally, reconstruction must retain higher products whenever the formality obstruction prevents their removal.

1

The reconstruction problem

A quantum field theory assigns measurements to regions of space. Two measurements in disjoint regions can be combined. As their positions approach one another, their product can develop a singularity. The coefficients of that singularity record interactions, symmetries and the action of one measurement on another.

This programme asks how much of a theory those local products determine. Its central problem is an associative form of chiral Koszul duality: a construction that passes between two associative algebras while retaining the positions of insertions and their collision laws. Quantum groups describe compatible ways to multiply, split and exchange these insertions. Holographic reconstruction asks whether observables on a boundary, together with their actions and states, recover a theory in the region it bounds.

The constructions have several domains. Some concern algebraic fields on a complex curve. Others retain the geometry of several colliding points, operations along a real direction, or coefficients arising from moduli spaces and arithmetic. The maps between these domains carry the substance of the comparison. Their hypotheses determine which products, singularities, states and symmetries can be recovered.

2

A current and its vacuum

An observable is a quantity assigned to fields in a region. In a classical theory it is a function of the fields. In a quantum theory observables form an algebra, and their multiplication records the order of measurements. An operator field packages operators that depend on an insertion point.

Consider a current J(z)J(z) depending on a complex coordinate zz, with singular product

J(z)J(w)∼κ(z−w)2𝟏.J(z)J(w)\sim\frac{\kappa}{(z-w)^2}\,\mathbf 1.

Here κ\kappa is a scalar called the level, 𝟏\mathbf 1 is the identity insertion, and ∼\sim specifies the singular part of the product. The double pole is observable even in a state whose expectation of each individual current is zero.

Expand the current into modes, the coefficients in its Laurent series,

J(z)=∑n∈ℤJnz−n−1.J(z)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}J_nz^{-n-1}.

The residue of a Laurent differential is the coefficient of z−1dzz^{-1}dz. Taking residues of the double pole gives

[Jm,Jn]=κmδm+n,01,[J_m,J_n]=\kappa m\,\delta_{m+n,0}\,1,

where [A,B]=AB−BA[A,B]=AB-BA is the commutator and the Kronecker symbol δr,0\delta_{r,0} is one for r=0r=0 and zero otherwise. These are the Heisenberg relations. They recover an algebra of operators from the singularity of two fields.

Over a coefficient field kk of characteristic zero, the vacuum representation is the polynomial space

Vκ=k[x1,x2,…],J−n=xn,Jn=κn∂∂xn(n>0).V_\kappa=k[x_1,x_2,\ldots], \qquad J_{-n}=x_n, \qquad J_n=\kappa n\frac{\partial}{\partial x_n} \quad(n>0).

Every polynomial uses finitely many variables. The zero mode acts by zero, and the vacuum is the constant polynomial 𝟏=1\mathbf 1=1. Negative modes create excitations. Positive modes remove them by differentiation. This representation is the vacuum Fock space.

The relation [J1,J−1]=κ1[J_1,J_{-1}]=\kappa1 also settles a distinction needed throughout the theory. An augmentation is a unital algebra homomorphism to the scalar field. At κ≠0\kappa\ne0, the mode algebra has no augmentation: scalar images commute, so such a homomorphism would imply 0=κ0=\kappa. The linear functional that extracts the constant term of a state nevertheless exists. It evaluates states without being a homomorphism from the mode algebra.

A prepared state specifies such an evaluation, together with the domain and physical data that make it meaningful. Its correlation functions are evaluations of products, for example

λ(J(z1)⋯J(zn)𝟏).\lambda\bigl(J(z_1)\cdots J(z_n)\mathbf 1\bigr).

The algebra determines how the operators compose. The vacuum determines their identity and creation property. The prepared state determines their numerical expectations. A reconstruction of physical correlation functions must supply all three.

3

Fields and exchange

The modes of one current generate fields for its polynomial descendants. Translation acts by Txn=nxn+1Tx_n=nx_{n+1} and the product rule. A vertex algebra consists of a state space VV, vacuum 𝟏\mathbf 1, translation TT, and fields

Y(a,z)b=∑n∈ℤ(a(n)b)z−n−1.Y(a,z)b=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}(a_{(n)}b)z^{-n-1}.

For each input pair, only finitely many negative powers occur. The vacuum satisfies Y(𝟏,z)=idY(\mathbf 1,z)=\mathrm{id} and Y(a,z)𝟏=ezTaY(a,z)\mathbf 1=e^{zT}a. Translation differentiates the field. Associativity compares the expansions of a three-field product in two orders of taking limits. Locality says that a sufficiently large power of z−wz-w kills the commutator of two fields. Odd states use the corresponding sign when exchanged.

A quantum vertex algebra has a specified exchange operator 𝒮(z)\mathcal S(z). Reversing two fields applies this operator to their states. Consistency requires three exchanges to satisfy the Yang–Baxter equation,

𝒮12(z1−z2)𝒮13(z1−z3)𝒮23(z2−z3)=𝒮23(z2−z3)𝒮13(z1−z3)𝒮12(z1−z2).\begin{aligned} &\mathcal S_{12}(z_1-z_2)\mathcal S_{13}(z_1-z_3) \mathcal S_{23}(z_2-z_3)\\ &\qquad= \mathcal S_{23}(z_2-z_3)\mathcal S_{13}(z_1-z_3) \mathcal S_{12}(z_1-z_2). \end{aligned}

The subscripts indicate which two factors are exchanged. In the convention Yz=ezTY−z𝒮(−z)τY_z=e^{zT}Y_{-z}\mathcal S(-z)\tau, with τ\tau the graded flip, the inversion and translation equations are 𝒮21(−z)𝒮(z)=1\mathcal S^{21}(-z)\mathcal S(z)=1 and [T⊗1,𝒮(z)]=−∂z𝒮(z)[T\otimes1,\mathcal S(z)]=-\partial_z\mathcal S(z). Exchange must also preserve the vacuum and commute with forming a product. The latter condition is a hexagon identity: exchanging one insertion with a product agrees with exchanging it successively with the two factors.

A free example makes the exchange visible. Keep the polynomial states and translation above, but take the contraction

P(u)=κu2+λuover k[κ,λ].P(u)=\frac{\kappa}{u^2}+\frac{\lambda}{u} \quad\text{over }k[\kappa,\lambda].

A contraction is the scalar term contributed when two fields are paired in their product. The even pole is unchanged when the separation uu is reversed. The odd pole changes sign.

Write ∂p=∂/∂xp\partial_p=\partial/\partial x_p, let μ\mu multiply polynomials, and set

Kpq(u)=(−1)q−1P(p+q−2)(u)(p−1)!(q−1)!,C(u)=∑p,q≥1Kpq(u)∂p⊗∂q,Y(a,u)b=μ(euT⊗1)eC(u)(a⊗b).\begin{aligned} K_{pq}(u)&= \frac{(-1)^{q-1}P^{(p+q-2)}(u)}{(p-1)!(q-1)!},\\ C(u)&=\sum_{p,q\geq1}K_{pq}(u)\,\partial_p\otimes\partial_q,\\ Y(a,u)b&=\mu(e^{uT}\otimes1)e^{C(u)}(a\otimes b). \end{aligned}

The symbol ⊗\otimes keeps the two inputs independent until multiplication. Each contraction exponential terminates on polynomial inputs. The translation exponential is a formal power series: its coefficients determine the operation without a numerical convergence assertion.

Proposition

These formulas define a quantum vertex algebra with rational exchange

𝒮(u)=exp⁡(∑p,q≥1[Kqp(−u)−Kpq(u)]∂p⊗∂q).\mathcal S(u)= \exp\!\left( \sum_{p,q\geq1}[K_{qp}(-u)-K_{pq}(u)] \,\partial_p\otimes\partial_q \right).

Proof

Indeed, the derivatives in the exponent commute. Products of several fields therefore come from the exponential of the sum of all pair contractions. Exchanging two inputs replaces their contraction by the contraction at reversed separation. This proves the exchange relation. The same commutation gives the Yang–Baxter equation, and the product rule gives the hexagon identity.

For J=x1J=x_1, the exchange is

𝒮(u)(J⊗J)=J⊗J−2λu𝟏⊗𝟏.\mathcal S(u)(J\otimes J) =J\otimes J-\frac{2\lambda}{u}\,\mathbf 1\otimes\mathbf 1.

Thus an odd contraction produces a nonzero change in an actual field product. At λ=0\lambda=0, the exchange becomes the identity and the example is the Heisenberg vertex algebra. The dependence on separation will also matter when these fields are compared with quantum-group operations.

4

Collisions and insertion order

Products of several fields require more information than a list of occupied positions. On three insertions, the first and third can meet while the second remains separate. That middle insertion still acts. For elementary matrices,

E12E21E12=E12,E122=0.E_{12}E_{21}E_{12}=E_{12}, \qquad E_{12}^{2}=0.

Deleting the intervening factor changes the product. In a field theory the same issue involves positions and singular expansions as well as matrix multiplication.

A configuration space parametrizes distinct labelled points of a space XX. Its ambient space XnX^n also contains their collisions. The pair diagonal Δij\Delta_{ij} is the locus xi=xjx_i=x_j. A collision stratum specifies a complete pattern of equalities. An insertion kept while other insertions interact is a spectator. Its state and position remain inputs to the operation.

Two geometries organize this information. An ordered word records a sequence of positions, allowing adjacent equal entries to collapse. Thus abab, abaaba and abababab remain different when a≠ba\ne b. A cut separates a word into an initial and a final segment. The cut is allowed on the open set where every position in one segment differs from every position in the other.

The ordered collision atlas instead begins with a chart for each total order of a finite label set. Two charts agree wherever the pairs on which their orders differ are distinct. At a collision, the atlas retains an order within each group of coincident points. This construction supports decompositions into arbitrary subsets, while the word construction uses consecutive segments.

The choice affects the tensor product that combines coefficient systems. It also affects factorization, the requirement that coefficients over separated groups of positions agree with the tensor product of the coefficients for each group. A comparison between the two geometries must state which separating maps it preserves.

The identity for a cut product sits at the empty word. The local vacuum sits at a nonempty insertion. The Heisenberg example already shows why these units need separate definitions: a nonzero local vacuum can coexist with the obstruction to a scalar augmentation of its mode algebra.

5

Complexes and corrections

An operation may commute with another only up to a specified correction. To compose several such operations, one must retain the correction and the equations it satisfies.

A cochain complex is a graded vector space V=⨁iViV=\bigoplus_iV^i with maps d:Vi→Vi+1d:V^i\to V^{i+1} satisfying d2=0d^2=0. Its cohomology is

Hi(V)=ker⁡(d:Vi→Vi+1)im⁡(d:Vi−1→Vi).H^i(V)=\frac{\ker(d:V^i\to V^{i+1})} {\operatorname{im}(d:V^{i-1}\to V^i)}.

A homotopy between cochain maps ff and gg is a degree-minus-one map hh with f−g=dh+hdf-g=dh+hd. A quasi-isomorphism induces an isomorphism on every cohomology group. Derived constructions retain complexes up to these equivalences, including the homotopies needed to compare their operations.

The derived tensor product illustrates the extra information. Let R=k[u]R=k[u] and k=R/(u)k=R/(u). The resolution [R→uR][R\xrightarrow{u}R] gives

k⊗R𝕃k=[k→0k],k\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}k=[k\xrightarrow{0}k],

with nonzero terms in degrees −1-1 and 00. The negative-degree term records the intersection relation. Ordinary tensoring keeps only degree zero.

The same distinction matters for collisions. A differential module carries actions of both functions and differential operators. Along a collision it can retain derivatives transverse to the collision locus. Local cohomology retains the part of a complex supported on that locus, including degrees that an ordinary kernel would lose. These are the coefficient systems in which the singular products and their corrections can be compared.

The BRST construction introduces odd variables for infinitesimal symmetries and a differential encoding their action and relations. An explicit square shows why all mixed terms matter. Let c−1,c0c_{-1},c_0 act by exterior multiplication on k[x]⊗Λ(c−1,c0)k[x]\otimes\Lambda(c_{-1},c_0), and put

Q=c−1∂x+c0x.Q=c_{-1}\partial_x+c_0x.

Since the odd variables anticommute,

Q2=c−1c0[∂x,x]=c−1c0.Q^2=c_{-1}c_0[\partial_x,x]=c_{-1}c_0.

Each separate summand squares to zero. Their mixed term remembers the Heisenberg relation. A coupled differential must account for this term through the coefficient differential or a specified curvature. That requirement returns in the quantum master equation and in the comparison between boundary fields and bulk observables.

6

Associative duality

An associative product remembers the order of its inputs. To retain that order when points collide, one must specify both the coefficient space and the decompositions on which multiplication is defined. Two constructions do this in different ways. Throughout this comparison, the geometric base is smooth, separated and of finite type, with positive pure dimension over a field of characteristic zero.

The word construction assigns a complex of right differential modules to each ordered configuration on a smooth scheme XX. It identifies coefficients under monotone collisions, which collapse consecutive groups of positions. Its product sums over consecutive cuts. A cut after position pp uses the open set on which every point in the first block differs from every point in the second block; points within either block may coincide.

The collision-atlas construction keeps a chart for each total order of a finite set of labels. Two charts overlap wherever each pair whose order changes has distinct coordinates. Its convolution sums over all ordered subset decompositions. Thus its product can use a block such as {1,3}\{1,3\}, while a consecutive cut of the word 123123 cannot.

Both constructions adjoin the same kind of isolated empty unit KK: its coefficient is the ground field at the empty configuration and zero at every positive configuration. This unit differs from a local field vacuum, which lives at a point.

Let ⋆\star denote either of these specified convolutions. For an augmented associative algebra AA whose empty coefficient is the ground field, write a=fib⁡(A→K)a=\operatorname{fib}(A\to K). Its bar construction is BA=K⊕︎⨁r≥1(sa)⋆r.BA=K\oplus\bigoplus_{r\geq1}(sa)^{\star r}. Here ss is the bar suspension. The differential combines the coefficient differential with multiplication of adjacent entries. The coproduct cuts each word into an initial and a final segment. For a coaugmented coassociative coalgebra CC, with reduced part c=cofib⁡(K→C)c=\operatorname{cofib}(K\to C), the cobar construction has the inverse shift tt: ΩC=K⊕︎⨁r≥1(tc)⋆r.\Omega C=K\oplus\bigoplus_{r\geq1}(tc)^{\star r}. Its product concatenates words, and its differential splits an entry using the reduced coproduct.

Theorem

For augmented associative algebras and coaugmented coassociative coalgebras with scalar empty coefficient, bar and cobar give inverse equivalences on each of these collision carriers. The equivalences retain the operations, their coherent homotopies, and the collision maps.

Proof

Every reduced factor occupies a nonempty part of a configuration. At nn labels, a word with more than nn such factors vanishes. The apparently infinite bar and cobar expressions are therefore finite at each configuration.

In the composite ΩBA\Omega BA, flatten a term into its original algebra entries. Each gap between adjacent entries has two states: it lies inside one bar block, or between two cobar factors. After filtering by the number of original entries, changing a gap gives a two-term identity complex. A word with more than one entry has at least one such contractible factor. Only the empty word and the single-entry term survive. The same argument, with the opposite filtration, applies to BΩCB\Omega C. The filtrations are finite at every configuration, so the comparison maps are equivalences. The enhanced bar and cobar construction supplies their coherent triangle identities.

This argument explains why no additional global elementwise conilpotence assumption is needed here. The bound comes from the number of occupied labels. It does not bound the cohomological degrees of an individual coefficient complex.

Partial collisions

Passing between the two carriers requires more than exchanging fields at pairwise distinct points. The word charts 123123 and 132132 overlap along the partial collision x1=x3≠x2x_1=x_3\ne x_2. In the first chart, the equal labels are separated by a cut; in the second, they form the consecutive block 1313.

This distinction produces an obstruction. Suppose the positive coefficients of a cut algebra are supported on the small diagonals, with singleton coefficient MM, and suppose M⊠MM\boxtimes M is nonzero away from the diagonal in X2X^2. On the displayed partial collision, the bar in chart 123123 restricts to zero. In chart 132132, the two-block term [13|2][13|2] survives. These restrictions cannot be identified. The resulting word bar therefore has no extension to the full collision atlas under those hypotheses.

A comparison holds when the word coefficients carry full-overlap exchange: equivalences between every pair of overlapping order charts, with coherent cocycles and compatibility with monotone collisions. Descent then recovers the collision coefficients. If the exchange also preserves the strong cut coproducts, it recovers the componentwise strong coproduct for arbitrary ordered subset decompositions.

“Componentwise strong” means that the map for each fixed decomposition is an equivalence on its own disjoint open. It does not say that the combined map to the sum of all decomposition terms is an equivalence. Even when two component maps are both the identity of a nonzero object VV, the combined diagonal V→V⊕︎VV\to V\oplus V is not an equivalence.

There are also structured comparisons without exchange. Including consecutive bar words gives a map from the cut bar of the restricted algebra to the restriction of its atlas bar. Projecting cobar words onto consecutive words gives a map in the opposite direction for cobar. These maps need not be equivalences. Already at two positions, the cobar projection omits a reverse-order term supported on the distinct-point open. Projecting bar words in the reverse direction generally fails even to be a chain map: it can erase a reversed two-entry word while retaining that word’s one-entry multiplication face.

The Lie–commutative comparison

On the nonempty Ran space, chiral Lie–coalgebra duality compares chiral Lie algebras with cocommutative chiral coalgebras. Its restriction to Lie objects supported on the main diagonal gives factorizing coalgebras. This is a different equivalence from the associative bar–cobar construction.

On the affine line, the comparison is concrete. Pull a chiral Lie algebra LL back to the ordered collision atlas, form its associative envelope U⋆(q!L)U_\star(q^!L), and adjoin the empty coaugmentation to its pulled-back Chevalley chains. There is a natural equivalence K⊕︎q!Cch(L)≃B(U⋆(q!L)).K\oplus q^!C^{\mathrm{ch}}(L) \simeq B\bigl(U_\star(q^!L)\bigr). For an abelian degree-zero two-input example, it sends the suspended symmetric class sx1sx2sx_1\,sx_2 to [x1|x2]−[x2|x1][x_1|x_2]-[x_2|x_1], with no factor of 1/21/2. Both words are needed: discarding one retains its nonzero multiplication differential and fails to define a chain map.

In the reverse direction, an ordered algebra AA must be supplied with a factorizing Ran coalgebra DD and an equivalence K⊕︎q!D≃BAK\oplus q^!D\simeq BA preserving the full cocommutative structure and collision descent. Only then can chiral primitives be applied to DD. Generic exchange does not construct this descent, and the isolated empty coaugmentation does not supply a local vertex vacuum.

7

Coefficient duality

Bar and cobar compare associative algebras with coassociative coalgebras. To obtain another associative algebra, one must also dualize the coefficients. The choice of dual matters: an internal dual into the isolated empty unit loses all positive configurations, while a dual formed chart by chart can retain them.

Bounded holonomic differential modules admit Verdier duality. Under this duality, a convolution assembled with open direct images j∗j_* becomes one assembled with j!j_!. This gives an associative algebra duality on that coefficient domain. Full current fields usually lie outside it. On the affine line, a current generated by a state φ\varphi with linearly independent translates TnφT^n\varphi is a free rank-one differential module. Its characteristic variety is the whole cotangent bundle, so it is not holonomic. Keeping finitely many translates also fails to give a translation-stable subspace.

Finite projective resolution is a different condition, and the free current satisfies it. On a smooth affine chart UU of dimension dd, put R=Γ(U,𝒟U)R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal D_U). A perfect right RR-complex is a retract of a finite complex of finite-rank free modules. With a coordinate volume form, its dual is P†=(RHomR⁡(P,R))t[d],P^\dagger=\bigl(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,R)\bigr)^t[d], where formal transpose sends ∂i\partial_i to −∂i-\partial_i and converts the left dual module back to a right module. The canonical line gives the coordinate-independent conversion.

For a derived module presented as a filtered colimit M≃colimα⁡PαM\simeq\operatorname{colim}_\alpha P_\alpha of perfect complexes, retain the inverse diagram M♯={Pα†}αin Pro⁡(Perfr⁡(R)).M^\sharp=\{P_\alpha^\dagger\}_\alpha \quad\text{in }\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{Perf}_r(R)). The perfect stages need not be submodules of MM. A pro-perfect coefficient retains the stages and transition maps, with the pro-category’s mapping spaces. Its inverse dual is 𝖲{Qβ}=colimβ⁡Qβ†\mathsf S\{Q_\beta\}=\operatorname{colim}_\beta Q_\beta^\dagger.

Theorem

Coefficient transposition gives a contravariant equivalence between derived differential-module coefficients and pro-perfect coefficients. Applied on every chart with the coordinate and collision comparisons retained, it transports the geometric operations as well as their underlying objects.

Proof

For N=colimβ⁡QβN=\operatorname{colim}_\beta Q_\beta, the mapping-space formula is MapPro⁡⁡(N♯,M♯)≃limα⁡colimβ⁡Map⁡(Pα,Qβ)≃Map⁡(M,N).\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Pro}}(N^\sharp,M^\sharp) \simeq\lim_\alpha\operatorname{colim}_\beta \operatorname{Map}(P_\alpha,Q_\beta) \simeq\operatorname{Map}(M,N). Finite projective biduality gives the first equivalence; compactness of the perfect stages gives the second. Every inverse diagram of perfect complexes is obtained by dualizing the filtered colimit of its dual stages. These comparisons also establish independence of the chosen presentation.

The retained inverse diagram cannot generally be replaced by its ordinary inverse limit. For the first Weyl algebra R=k⟨u,∂⟩/(∂u−u∂−1),R=k\langle u,\partial\rangle/(\partial u-u\partial-1), localization has the presentation R[u−1]=colim⁡(R→LuR→Lu⋯)R[u^{-1}]=\operatorname{colim}(R\xrightarrow{L_u}R\xrightarrow{L_u}\cdots), where LuL_u is left multiplication by uu. Its dual is the inverse diagram with the same transition map on R[1]R[1]. This pro-object is nonzero: no sufficiently long transition is zero. Its ordinary inverse limit vanishes, because a compatible element would lie in ⋂n≥0unR=0\bigcap_{n\geq0}u^nR=0. This calculation concerns the ordinary limit; it makes no assertion that the derived inverse limit vanishes.

The dual product

Write 𝒞♯\mathcal C^\sharp for the pro-perfect collision category and 𝖲\mathsf S for inverse coefficient duality. Its transported convolution is E⋆♯F=(𝖲E⋆𝖲F)♯.E\star_\sharp F=(\mathsf S E\star\mathsf S F)^\sharp. For an open immersion jj and a collision map δ\delta, the corresponding functors are ♯j∗𝖲\sharp j_*\mathsf S and ♯δ!𝖲\sharp\delta^!\mathsf S. These formulas specify functors in the new coefficient category. They do not assume that ordinary shriek extension exists on arbitrary differential modules.

For an augmented collision algebra AA with scalar empty coefficient, define 𝖪♯A=(BA)♯.\mathsf K_\sharp A=(BA)^\sharp. Its multiplication is the transpose of bar deconcatenation, and its unit and augmentation transpose the bar counit and coaugmentation. Coefficient transposition and the finite bar–cobar equivalence give an anti-equivalence of augmented associative algebras for ⋆\star and ⋆♯\star_\sharp. The inverse is E⟼𝖲B⋆♯E,𝖲B⋆♯((BA)♯)≃ΩBA≃A.E\longmapsto\mathsf S B_{\star_\sharp}E, \qquad \mathsf S B_{\star_\sharp}\bigl((BA)^\sharp\bigr) \simeq\Omega BA\simeq A. This construction retains full current coefficients, ordered collision maps, and normal derivatives. It establishes an associative-to-associative duality in the two stated coefficient categories.

A second system of state fields requires additional structure. In particular, not every geometric dual has the singleton coefficient of a current. A square-zero collision algebra can have its entire positive part supported where all points equal a fixed point of the line. Its dual singleton remains nonzero and point-supported. Such a coefficient cannot be identified, even after a cohomological shift, with ωX⊗V\omega_X\otimes V for a state complex with nonzero cohomology: the latter has full support and is torsion-free over functions. Field realization must therefore specify an appropriate domain, translation, singular operations, and local vacuum maps.

A field realization

There is a field realization of full coefficient duality on a class with commuting jet contractions. Work over ℂ\mathbb C at each finite formal precision ℂ[ℏ]/(ℏr)\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^r), with compatible reduction maps. Start from A=SymR⁡(E⊗ℂℂ[t])/𝔞,A=\operatorname{Sym}_R(E\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[t])/\mathfrak a, where RR is a finite-dimensional commutative unital algebra, EE is a bounded nonpositive complex of finite-dimensional RR-modules, and the relation ideal is homogeneous in charge and weight, has positive charge, and is preserved by the differential, translation, and commuting jet derivations.

The construction uses two related field objects. The original state algebra AA carries quantum vertex fields. A second object consists of meromorphic Chevalley cochains of the current Lie algebra 𝔰𝔩2⊗A\mathfrak{sl}_2\otimes A. It retains its finite-weight polynomial core, charge decomposition, and jet actions as marked structure. Its constituent jet variables are localized jointly along their discriminants. These variables are different from the positions on the underlying curve.

A scalar pair factor w(u)∈1+ℏℂ[u,u−1][[ℏ]]w(u)\in1+\hbar\mathbb C[u,u^{-1}][[\hbar]] determines the interaction. If ℓ(u)=log⁡w(u)\ell(u)=\log w(u) and δi\delta_i are the commuting jet derivations, put Cℓ(u)=∑p,q≥0(−1)qℓ(p+q)(u)p!q!δp+1⊗δq+1,E(u)=e−Cℓ(u).C_\ell(u)=\sum_{p,q\geq0} \frac{(-1)^q\ell^{(p+q)}(u)}{p!q!} \delta_{p+1}\otimes\delta_{q+1}, \qquad E(u)=e^{-C_\ell(u)}. Then the original fields and exchange are YAw(a,u)b=μA(euT⊗1)E(u)(a⊗b),𝒮Aw(u)=E21(−u)E(u)−1.Y_A^w(a,u)b=\mu_A(e^{uT}\otimes1)E(u)(a\otimes b), \qquad \mathcal S_A^w(u)=E^{21}(-u)E(u)^{-1}. At finite formal precision, the exponential has finitely many terms. On any fixed input, only finitely many jet lowerings contribute. This supplies the required finite pole bound for each input.

The cochain object has its own product, defined before comparison with geometric coefficients. Between groups of constituent variables xix_i and yjy_j, its multiplier is a product of factors w(u+xi−yj)w(u+x_i-y_j) on their joint localization. Expanding its logarithm and transposing the constituent multiplications recovers exactly Cℓ(u)C_\ell(u). This calculation identifies the source product with the transpose of the current collision coproduct.

Theorem

On this marked charged-jet class, the meromorphic cochain construction admits a covariant strong monoidal coefficient functor. Its native product is identified with the multiplication of the full coefficient dual of the original current collision coalgebra. The comparison retains both orders, arbitrary ordered subset decompositions, every normal derivative and spectator, and both local vacuum actions.

Proof

The pair contractions are horizontal for the combined geometric and state translation. They therefore extend over the full differential-module transfer along collisions. A contraction with a product separates into contractions with its two factors. Consequently either association of three inputs has the same three commuting pair factors.

For an ordered decomposition into groups G,HG,H, the full contraction factors into the contractions internal to GG, internal to HH, and the cross factor EG,HE_{G,H}. The inverse cross factor supplies the tensor comparison. With three groups, both composite comparisons contain the same product of three cross factors, which proves monoidal coherence. Changing order and then merging gives the same identity for a nonconsecutive merger such as 13|213|2. Taking full principal parts retains the normal-transfer module, so the calculation does not discard higher normal derivatives.

The field tensor unit maps to the isolated empty unit. The scalar-current object instead carries the local vacuum coefficient. A specified augmentation R→ℂR\to\mathbb C gives a section of its local projection. These are separate maps. Applying coefficient duality twice returns the complete collision coefficient system; it does not assert vector-space biduality for the meromorphic state space.

Markings and automorphisms

The marked structure cannot simply be omitted from a recognition claim. Consider the charged jet quotient A=ℂ[e0,e1,e2,…]/(e0,e1,e2,…)3,Ten=(n+1)en+1.A=\mathbb C[e_0,e_1,e_2,\ldots]/(e_0,e_1,e_2,\ldots)^3, \qquad Te_n=(n+1)e_{n+1}. All jet indices remain; only charge at least three is killed. With w(u)=1−ℏ/uw(u)=1-\hbar/u, the finite exponential ψ=exp⁡(ℏT)\psi=\exp(\hbar T) acts on every collision coefficient. It preserves the product, exchange, cuts, translation, scalar maps, both vacua, and all supported normal-transfer maps. Yet it does not preserve the designated jet derivation δ2\delta_2: the relation [δ2,T]=N[\delta_2,T]=N, where NN counts charge, gives a nonzero first-order discrepancy. Thus an automorphism of the unmarked full coefficient algebra need not lift to the marked cochain object.

A current framing supplies the identification of the singleton coefficient with ωX⊗A\omega_X\otimes A. For coefficient maps that are constant in this framing, the original fields can be recovered from their contact maps by a(n)b=[u−1]rY(un;a,b),Y(a,u)b=∑n∈ℤ(a(n)b)u−n−1.a_{(n)}b=[u^{-1}]\,r_Y(u^n;a,b), \qquad Y(a,u)b=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}(a_{(n)}b)u^{-n-1}. On the specified essential image, this recovery retains translation and both vacuum equations. For an actual isomorphism of recovered charged state algebras, a constant horizontal singleton that preserves charge and the scalar maps lifts to the marked construction exactly when it also preserves δ2\delta_2; these conditions force preservation of all the jet derivations. This is a criterion for the supplied state map, not a replacement for constructing a derived lift from cohomology data.

The result therefore gives a positive field realization with an explicit tensor comparison, together with a concrete reason its marked hypotheses matter. Intrinsic recognition after forgetting the current structure, and realization for general nonabelian exchange, require additional constructions.

Currents and ghosts

The Heisenberg current at level κ\kappa has modes [Jm,Jn]=κmδm+n,0.[J_m,J_n]=\kappa m\,\delta_{m+n,0}. Its dual field description uses the commutative vertex superalgebra Λ[c]\Lambda[c] freely generated by one odd degree-one field, together with the curvature state wκ=κ2cTc.w_\kappa=\frac{\kappa}{2}c\,Tc. The curvature is essential. Although its zero mode vanishes on the ordinary ghost vacuum, it can act nontrivially on other ghost modules and retains the current level.

A curved commutative vertex algebra is a commutative differential graded vertex algebra (A,d)(A,d) with a degree-two state ww satisfying dw∈TAdw\in TA. A curved vertex module has a degree-one operator QQ with [Q,a(n)]=(da)(n),Q2=−w(0).[Q,a_{(n)}]=(da)_{(n)},\qquad Q^2=-w_{(0)}. Only the class of ww modulo total derivatives enters, because (Ta)(0)=0(Ta)_{(0)}=0. Such a module need not be a complex: its square can be nonzero. Maps between two modules at the same level do form a complex, since their equal curvature actions cancel in the square of the commutator differential.

Smoothness makes the action finite on each vector.

Theorem

The Heisenberg vertex algebra and the curved ghost algebra characterize one another through this coupling. A state jj in a degree-zero vertex algebra defines a morphism from the Heisenberg algebra at level κ\kappa exactly when j⊗cj\otimes c is a twisting state for (Λ[c],0,wκ)(\Lambda[c],0,w_\kappa). Conversely, an odd state c′c' in a curved commutative vertex algebra defines a morphism from (Λ[c],0,wκ)(\Lambda[c],0,w_\kappa) exactly when J⊗c′J\otimes c' is a twisting state.

The same construction works for a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with an invariant symmetric form gabg_{ab}. These are universal properties of fields and twisting states. Their ghost algebra is commutative because the original currents form a Lie algebra. A twisting state lies in a tensor product of field algebras; it is different from a bar twisting cochain whose source is a coalgebra.

Unbounded module complexes

Boundedness controls the totalization. Algebraic tail cochains use a direct sum over exterior degrees; product totalization allows infinitely many such degrees in one total degree. They agree for bounded-below inputs but can disagree otherwise.

Product totalization and recovery

For a current complex YY, the two tail constructions in total degree dd are Cp⊕︎(Y)d=⨁a≥0Yd−a⊗RΛRa(ξn:n≥p),CpΠ(Y)d=∏a≥0Yd−a⊗RΛRa(ξn:n≥p).C_p^\oplus(Y)^d=\bigoplus_{a\geq0} Y^{d-a}\otimes_R\Lambda_R^a(\xi_n:n\geq p), \qquad C_p^\Pi(Y)^d=\prod_{a\geq0} Y^{d-a}\otimes_R\Lambda_R^a(\xi_n:n\geq p). Each exterior-degree component retains finite algebraic support. The product permits infinitely many exterior degrees; it does not complete every ghost mode indiscriminately.

For the acyclic XX above, set Pr=∏i=1rηiξiP_r=\prod_{i=1}^r\eta_i\xi_i and P0=1P_0=1. The product totalization contains b=∑r≥1xrηrPr−1,db=∑r≥1(Pr−1−Pr)=1.b=\sum_{r\geq1}x_r\eta_rP_{r-1},\qquad db=\sum_{r\geq1}(P_{r-1}-P_r)=1. Every component is a finite monomial, while no finite partial sum has differential 11. More generally, the tail differential has a part preserving exterior degree and a part raising it. For an acyclic input, one solves for a primitive successively in exterior degree. The product admits the resulting sequence. Thus product tail cochains preserve acyclicity, and the smooth product transform descends to the ordinary unbounded derived category.

Its canonical recovery map can still fail. At κ=0\kappa=0, let Y−a=keaY^{-a}=ke_a for a≥0a\geq0, with zero differential and zero currents. The product vector whose exterior-degree-aa component is eaξaξa+1⋯ξ2a−1(a≥1)e_a\xi_a\xi_{a+1}\cdots\xi_{2a-1}\qquad(a\geq1) survives every finite erasure of low-index ghosts. It gives an extra degree-zero recovery class outside H0(Y)=ke0H^0(Y)=ke_0.

The old algebraic evaluation also need not extend, even as a cochain map. An algebraic ghost-linear projection from the transform of XX sends 11 to a nonzero vector in an independently defined zero-differential curved module. Product totalization makes that same 11 a boundary. Extending the projection would send a boundary to a nonzero vector in a zero-differential target, which is impossible; adjunction gives the corresponding obstruction to extending evaluation.

A product-based equivalence therefore needs a separately specified restricted or completed recipient and new recovery and evaluation comparisons. These zero-level examples decide the unrestricted integral assertion. They do not rule out a different flat or nonzero-level completed domain, whose continuous mapping objects, collision operations and sewing would have to be compared explicitly.

The stronger remaining comparison requires lifting γ\gamma and its Taylor gauge to operations compatible with the fixed transverse multiplication and boundary action. Wilson lines and connections

A pairing on affine cochains determines how finite Wilson modules move. Its coefficient is the inverse shifted level. The construction retains three different objects: cochains of a moving affine vacuum, a differential graded line algebra, and a connection on finite representation spaces. Their explicit operations provide part of the comparison with boundary fusion.

13Affine mergers and cobar comparison

Affine mergers

The ordinary affine residue merges two blocks of states. On a graded state space, a differential can also merge three or more blocks at once. There is an explicit polynomial family of such differentials in every arity. Its regular restriction has an invariant relative to the vacuum, but comparison of the associated cobars must also account for maps that change weights and composite states.

Let kk have characteristic zero, let 𝔤\mathfrak g be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with an invariant symmetric form BB, and put A=k[κ]A=k[\kappa]. Its PBW state module is V=A⊗kU(t−1𝔤[t−1])V=A\otimes_kU(t^{-1}\mathfrak g[t^{-1}]). Translation TT, the vacuum and the weights wt⁡(J−ra)=r\operatorname{wt}(J^a_{-r})=r are independent of the level. No simple quotient is taken. Quantum higher products

Cohomology retains the product of closed observables, but can lose their higher composition laws. An algebra is formal when a chain of multiplicative quasi-isomorphisms connects it to its cohomology algebra with zero differential. A nonzero value of one chosen higher product is insufficient to disprove formality: the value may change with the chosen contraction.

There is an invariant obstruction in a polynomial quantum reduction with three rotation coordinates. Work over R=ℂ[ℏ]R=\mathbb C[\hbar]. Take even variables xi,yix_i,y_i, antighosts ψi\psi_i of degree minus one, and ghosts γi\gamma^i of degree one, for 1≤i≤31\le i\le3. The even variables commute with the ghosts.

Let ϵijk\epsilon_{ijk} be the alternating tensor with ϵ123=1\epsilon_{123}=1. The rotation moments and BRST charge are μi=ϵijkxjyk,Θ=γiμi−12ϵijkγiγjψk,Q=ℏ−1[Θ,−]gr.\mu_i=\epsilon_{ijk}x_jy_k,\qquad \Theta=\gamma^i\mu_i-\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}\gamma^i\gamma^j\psi_k, \qquad Q=\hbar^{-1}[\Theta,-]_{\mathrm{gr}}. Every numerator is divisible by ℏ\hbar, so this formula defines a polynomial operator even at ℏ=0\hbar=0. The moment relations and the Jacobi identity give Q2=0Q^2=0.

A polynomial contraction computes the cohomology algebra as Z=Λ(χ)⊗(Wℏ(s,t)⊗Λ(θ))ℤ/2,[s,t]=ℏ,|θ|=−1,|χ|=3.Z=\Lambda(\chi)\otimes \bigl(W_\hbar(s,t)\otimes\Lambda(\theta)\bigr)^{\mathbb Z/2}, \qquad [s,t]=\hbar,\quad |\theta|=-1,\quad |\chi|=3. Here Wℏ(s,t)W_\hbar(s,t) is the Weyl algebra. The involution negates s,t,θs,t,\theta. Cohomology occurs only in degrees −1,0,2,3-1,0,2,3. The contraction remains valid after every commutative scalar base change.

Theorem

This traceless absolute quantum algebra is not formal over ℂ[ℏ]\mathbb C[\hbar]. After a scalar change ℏ↦λ\hbar\mapsto\lambda, the same conclusion holds whenever λ2≠0\lambda^2\ne0. The obstruction allows arbitrary cohomology markings and does not require the quasi-isomorphisms to preserve units. At ℏ=0\hbar=0, a multiplicative formality comparison exists.

Proof

In any differential graded algebra, let closed U,CU,C represent classes of degrees −1,3-1,3. Suppose U2=dPU^2=dP and UC+CU=dJUC+CU=dJ. Then Ω=PC+CP+UJ+JU\Omega=PC+CP+UJ+JU is closed. When these two cohomology groups vanish, [Ω][\Omega] is therefore a natural single class under multiplicative quasi-isomorphisms. In a zero-differential algebra it is zero.

For the quantum reduction, take U=xiψi,C=γ1γ2γ3,P=0,J=ℏxiγi.U=x_i\psi_i,\qquad C=\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3,\qquad P=0,\qquad J=\hbar x_i\gamma^i. The Clifford relations give Ω=ℏ2∑ixi2.\Omega=\hbar^2\sum_i x_i^2. Its cohomology class is ℏ2s2\hbar^2s^2, which is nonzero in the polynomial Weyl basis. Since H−3=H1=0H^{-3}=H^1=0, no change of primitives or cohomology marking can remove it. The same basis argument applies after scalar change whenever λ2≠0\lambda^2\ne0.

At a nonzero square-zero value of λ\lambda, this detector vanishes. It does not decide formality there. The result concerns the stated polynomial traceless algebra. The relative reduction, full scalar factors and other completions retain their separate comparison problems.

Modules and centres

An algebra duality acquires geometric content through its modules and their compositions. A boundary state is acted on by insertions at moving points; an interface carries commuting actions from its two sides. These structures require their own comparison maps.

For augmented collision algebras A,BA,B, put CA=BAC_A=BA and CB=BBC_B=BB. An AA–BB bimodule MM has the two-sided bar transform 𝔅A,B(M)=CA⋆M⋆CB,\mathfrak B_{A,B}(M)=C_A\star M\star C_B, with twisting terms from the two endpoint actions. The two twists anticommute because the actions commute. This gives a bicomodule over CA,CBC_A,C_B, and inverse twisting recovers the original bimodule.

Composition is retained by an explicit common complex. If NN is a BB–DD bimodule, then CA⋆M⋆CB⋆N⋆CDC_A\star M\star C_B\star N\star C_D represents both the bar transform of the derived balanced tensor M⋆B𝕃NM\star_B^{\mathbb L}N and the derived cotensor of the two transformed bicomodules. The comparison inserts the coproduct of the middle factor CBC_B. Its inverse on the cofree equalizer uses the counit, and a finite filtration proves the derived comparison. All reduced bar factors still occupy distinct nonempty parts, so their number is bounded at each configuration even when the endpoint modules have nonzero empty components.

Coefficient transposition turns this into an anti-equivalence of the corresponding bimodule categories for the two associative dual algebras. It preserves identity interfaces and balanced composition, with its associativity coherences. An exterior tensor of field representations is a separately specified operation; identifying it with this balanced composition requires a comparison of their coefficient spaces and actions.

Rooted boundary modules

Fix the root at 00 on the affine line. A rooted coefficient system has a component for each ordered list of moving points, together with coherent collision maps. A final block may collapse into the root and be absorbed by its state. The component with no moving points is the state complex at the root.

The action product F⋆∗MF\star_*M separates an initial word from the remaining points and from the root. A rooted module has an action A⋆∗M→MA\star_*M\to M; a rooted comodule has a coaction N→C⋆∗NN\to C\star_*N. The latter separates an initial word from the rooted remainder.

For C=BcutAC=B_{\mathrm{cut}}A, the twisting bar and its inverse give an equivalence between rooted AA-modules and rooted CC-comodules. Transposing the coaction then gives M⟼(C⋆∗,τM)♯,M\longmapsto(C\star_{*,\tau}M)^\sharp, an anti-equivalence with modules over C♯C^\sharp in the pro-perfect rooted category. The insertion maps of the dual module are exactly the transposed components of the rooted coaction. Their compositions retain the order of the moving inputs.

This classification does not select a physical boundary object from AA alone. An independently specified boundary must supply the rooted comodule, or equivalently the action of the dual algebra, together with the geometric meaning of its root states. The classification then determines the corresponding original rooted module up to equivalence.

Two insertion products

The convolution ⋆\star combines families of points at disjoint positions. The diagonal tensor ⊗!\otimes^! instead places two families at the same positions, with one family after the other along the transverse line. They come from different operations on one external product: open extension from disjoint positions, and extraordinary restriction to a stacked collision branch. In the binary case, the localization triangle relates them through the residues on the two ordered diagonal branches. Their interchange map keeps common decompositions and is generally not invertible.

For the convolution-centre statement, use the presentable stable category of collision coefficient systems with its symmetric disjoint-configuration convolution. This product preserves colimits in each variable. Let AA be an associative algebra in that category. A coherent action is a module structure on AA in the category of associative algebras, with its specified unit and higher coherences. The universal actor is the convolution centre Z(A)Z(A). It represents V⟼MapA-A⁡(V⋆A,A).V\longmapsto\operatorname{Map}_{A\text{-}A}(V\star A,A). Its composition operations give an E2E_2-algebra, and its evaluation is final among coherent convolution actions on AA. Every such action has a classifying map to Z(A)Z(A), unique up to a contractible space of choices. The centre acts naturally on each AA-module by composing its action on the regular bimodule with balanced tensor product. The empty component is only the scalar part of this object; the full centre has coefficients on all configurations.

For transverse actions, consider the category of connected coaugmented coassociative collision coalgebras with its diagonal tensor. A transverse monoid is an associative algebra object in that category. Its multiplication uses ⊗!\otimes^!, and its unit is the scalar-current coalgebra JJ. The closed structure gives a mapping coalgebra and hence a universal transverse monoid ℰ(C)=Hom⁡Coalg,⊗!(C,C).\mathcal E(C)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathrm{Coalg},\,\otimes^!}(C,C). Maps of transverse monoids into ℰ(C)\mathcal E(C) classify their transverse actions on CC. At a singleton, it is the pointwise internal endomorphism object of C1C_1. The universal object exists in the ambient coalgebra category; factorization of ℰ(C)\mathcal E(C) is an additional property.

Finality of factorizing actions

Restricting the actors to factorizing coalgebras changes the universal problem. Let QQ be a unital vertex algebra over ℂ\mathbb C, concentrated in cohomological degree zero, with algebraic state space. Let CQC_Q be its ordinary factorization coalgebra on the full ordered collision carrier. Allow connected, coaugmented, counital factorizing coalgebras as actors, with coherent unital transverse monoid structures and all their action homotopies. Impose no augmentation to JJ or extra propagation condition on an arbitrary actor.

Theorem

If QQ has a nonzero vertex derivation, this category of transverse monoid actions on CQC_Q has no final object. The obstruction allows unbounded derived receiving actors.

A vertex derivation DD kills the vacuum, commutes with translation, and satisfies the Leibniz identity for every vertex product. The obstruction constructs two parallel morphisms of actions. Equalizing them would kill a commutator operation, but its binary coefficient detects the nonzero derivation. That coefficient survives every allowed homotopy into a receiving factorizing action. A final object would have to equalize the pair, which is impossible.

The hypothesis has a clear boundary. For the scalar vertex algebra Q=ℂQ=\mathbb C, every derivation is zero and the final transverse action is JJ itself. The nonexistence theorem also leaves the ambient mapping coalgebra ℰ(CQ)\mathcal E(C_Q) and the convolution centre intact: each solves its own universal problem. Any proposed bulk-to-centre identification must specify which tensor, which class of actors, and which action comparison it uses.

Centres and boundary actions

A centre records operations together with their compositions. Its value therefore depends on the category of coefficients and on the tensor used to act. Three constructions make this dependence concrete: Morita invariance for convolution, a low-degree comparison of the Heisenberg scalar centres, and the characteristic map from a transverse action to a map of boundary modules.

Let (𝒞B,⋆,KB)(\mathcal C_B,\star,K_B) be the symmetric convolution category of differential-module coefficients on ordered collision schemes, over a characteristic-zero coefficient ring BB. A coefficient-linear functor satisfies coherent equivalences F(W⋆M)≃W⋆F(M)F(W\star M)\simeq W\star F(M) for every coefficient object WW, compatibly with the product and unit. Suppose that FF preserves colimits. Evaluating it on the free module AA gives a bimodule P=F(A)P=F(A), and applying FF to the free bar resolution constructs F(M)≃P⋆A𝕃M.F(M)\simeq P\star_A^{\mathbb L}M. This comparison also identifies natural transformations and their homotopies.

Endomorphisms of one selected vacuum module are a different recipient.

It includes length zero and uses product totalization. The cup product cuts a bar word into two pieces and evaluates a cochain on each piece. A lift to the two-sided bar resolution identifies this cup with derived composition. Braces insert cochains into ordered, disjoint slots, with the Koszul signs of the suspended inputs; their sums are finite at each input arity. The first brace is a binary insertion operation, distinct from the unary bar differential.

These operations can distinguish centres with the same apparent product data. For the square-zero algebra K⊕︎ιordω𝔸1K\oplus\iota_{\mathrm{ord}}\omega_{\mathbb A^1}, a binary operation complex contributes classes μ,ν\mu,\nu in centre degrees two and three. Indeed, on an arity-qq cochain the output contributes once and the inputs contribute qq times, giving [δ,f]G=(1−q)f[\delta,f]_{\mathrm G}=(1-q)f. The binary complex is only one part of the centre.

Matrix invariance preserves these operations explicitly. The map from cochains of AA to those of Mn(A)M_n(A) sums over matrix-index paths: (Φnf)(X1,…,Xq)i0iq=∑i1,…,iq−1f((X1)i0i1,…,(Xq)iq−1iq).(\Phi_n f)(X_1,\ldots,X_q)_{i_0i_q} =\sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_{q-1}} f\bigl((X_1)_{i_0i_1},\ldots,(X_q)_{i_{q-1}i_q}\bigr). Concatenating paths preserves cup; inserting paths preserves every brace. The corner bimodules Mn(A)e11M_n(A)e_{11} and e11Mn(A)e_{11}M_n(A) give the inverse Morita comparison. If A⌀=BA_\varnothing=B, then Mn(A)⌀=Mn(B)M_n(A)_\varnothing=M_n(B). For n>1n>1, its cochains therefore require the unnormalized bar or normalization relative to this separable matrix coefficient. The full derivation kernel

A chiral derivation is a differential-module endomorphism of 𝒱κ\mathscr V_\kappa that obeys the derivation identity for every residue, including every localized multiplier. Define 𝒦ij(P)=∑s=12∑m≥11(m−1)!(gisλm∂Pj∂xms−gjs(−λ−∇)m∂Pi∂xms).\mathcal K_{ij}(P)= \sum_{s=1}^{2}\sum_{m\geq1}\frac{1}{(m-1)!} \left( g_{is}\lambda^m\frac{\partial P_j}{\partial x^s_m} - g_{js}(-\lambda-\nabla)^m \frac{\partial P_i}{\partial x^s_m} \right). Put 𝔡B={P∈B[z,xmi]2:κ𝒦ij(P)=0 for all i,j}.\mathfrak d_B= \{P\in B[z,x^i_m]^2:\kappa\mathcal K_{ij}(P)=0 \text{ for all }i,j\}.

Theorem

Both scalar centres satisfy H0=BH^0=B and H1=𝔡BH^1=\mathfrak d_B. The degree-zero comparison is the scalar unit. The degree-one comparison and its inverse recover the derivation at one position and extend it to the collision envelope or by a sum over the state blocks of every word partition. They preserve the commutator bracket.

The degree bounds in the bar models explain why this is the full degree-one group. Positive cochains have degree at least one, and lengths at least two have degree at least two. Degree one can therefore contain only endomorphisms of equal partition coefficients. Residue compatibility determines these maps from their singleton derivation. The only length-zero coefficients are scalars, whose differential is zero, so there is no quotient by nonscalar inner derivations.

The constant linear substitutions Pi=∑jMijx1jP_i=\sum_jM_{ij}x^j_1 form the subspace κ(Mg+gM𝗍)=0.\kappa(Mg+gM^{\mathsf t})=0. It is the orthogonal Lie algebra at nonzero field-valued level and all endomorphisms at zero. It is a small part of 𝔡B\mathfrak d_B. Already Pi=fi(z)P_i=f_i(z) gives a class for every pair of polynomials, with δPxmi=fi(m−1)(z)(m−1)!𝟏.\delta_Px^i_m=\frac{f_i^{(m-1)}(z)}{(m-1)!}\mathbf1. Thus degree one is infinite-dimensional over kk. On the nonconsecutive partition 13|213|2, the extension acts on both the merged block and the spectator. For a hyperbolic pair with δa=a\delta a=a, δb=−b\delta b=-b, the residue of v−1a⊠𝟏v^{-1}a\boxtimes\mathbf1 is [v−1]a[v^{-1}]a. Its derivation identity needs the action on the spectator carrying aa.

The central term lies in the positive local vacuum line. It cannot be replaced by κ\kappa times the empty-word unit: applying the augmentation to that proposed relation would give 0=κ0=\kappa. Nor can the full state module be replaced by two diagonal generators. The comparison also has a specialization boundary. For g=I2g=I_2, the Euler image Pi=x1iP_i=x^i_1 gives κ𝒦ij=2κλδij\kappa\mathcal K_{ij}=2\kappa\lambda\delta_{ij}; it is allowed at level zero but does not extend to a class over k[κ]k[\kappa].

Degree-two words and their common sector

Let 𝒱π\mathcal V_\pi be the localized differential-module coefficient of a finite partition π\pi, with its Heisenberg residue maps rπ;ijr_{\pi;ij} merging two blocks. Consider families of single-merger variations hπ;ij:𝒱π⟶𝒱π/(i∼j).h_{\pi;ij}:\mathcal V_\pi\longrightarrow \mathcal V_{\pi/(i\sim j)} . Let ℜB\mathfrak R_B consist of the families for which replacing every residue by r+ϵhr+\epsilon h, with ϵ2=0\epsilon^2=0, preserves the square-zero residue differential, its cut coproduct and every monotone collision map. These are linear equations: the disjoint-pair and three-block residue identities linearized in ϵ\epsilon, together with cut and collision compatibility. All finite words occur. No fixed-vacuum or skew-symmetry condition is imposed on hh.

Let 𝔊B\mathfrak G_B consist of collision-compatible endomorphisms ψπ\psi_\pi additive across each admissible cut, with empty component zero. Their effect on the residues is (∂ψ)π;ij=rπ;ijψπ−ψπ/(i∼j)rπ;ij.(\partial\psi)_{\pi;ij} =r_{\pi;ij}\psi_\pi -\psi_{\pi/(i\sim j)}r_{\pi;ij}. The degree bounds leave only single-merger maps and self-extensions of equal partition coefficients. Inserting the undeformed vacuum at a new position, with a simple-pole multiplier, splits those module extensions. Induction over partitions reduces every class to a variation of the residues on the fixed modules. The remaining equations are exactly those defining ℜB\mathfrak R_B.

A substantial part of this quotient has an intrinsic comparison with the collision centre. Let 𝒬B\mathcal Q_B be the space of finite polynomial bilinear forms Q(λ)=∑d≥0Cdλd,Q(λ)=−Q(−λ)𝗍.Q(\lambda)=\sum_{d\geq0}C_d\lambda^d,\qquad Q(\lambda)=-Q(-\lambda)^{\mathsf t}. Finite Wick expansions construct it on every state, not only on the two currents. No completion in pole order, state degree or exterior degree is taken, and conformal-weight preservation is not imposed.

The central and cup classes have different detectors. Antisymmetrized products of derivations remain independent on two distinct positions; on the collision envelope their symbols have PBW degree two. Central variations take values in the primitive vacuum line. At level zero their normal principal parts are ∑dd!(Cd)ij[u−d−1]𝟏.\sum_d d!(C_d)_{ij}[u^{-d-1}]\mathbf1. Every undeformed field is then regular, so a change of state coordinates cannot produce these poles. A polynomial change of currents gives, on the two carriers, bNQ=κΓQw,dNQ=κΓQc.bN_Q=\kappa\Gamma_Q^{\mathrm w},\qquad dN_Q=\kappa\Gamma_Q^{\mathrm c}. The pole detector proves that the kernel is exactly κ𝒬B\kappa\mathcal Q_B.

Thus all central-polynomial classes disappear at nonzero field-valued level, while every QQ survives at zero. Derivation cups remain: polynomial translation derivations already give infinitely many independent degree-two classes at every level. Over k[κ]k[\kappa], variations of the symmetric pairing form only the three-dimensional κ\kappa-torsion part λSym2⁡(k2)∗\lambda\operatorname{Sym}^2(k^2)^*. A cubic polynomial Q=λ3HQ=\lambda^3H with HH symmetric supplies the additional fourth-order pole 6ϵH/u46\epsilon H/u^4 and lies outside the span of pairing variations and derivation cups.

The two injections identify their images, including the degree-one Gerstenhaber action on the exterior-square summand. They do not identify the full degree-two groups or assert that arbitrary nonlinear derivations preserve the central-polynomial summand. The remaining problem is to describe the additional classes in the full residue quotient and extend the comparison to them. These scalar centres also have a different cochain domain from bounded vertex cohomology, where a derivation-modulo-inner-derivation quotient may occur.

The two evaluations

The distinction between scalar and positive coefficients is decisive even in degree zero. Let VV be a nonzero unital vertex algebra in degree zero on the affine line, let A=U⋆LVA=U_\star L_V, and let WW be a coefficient system in the heart. Then H0Map𝒞⁡(W,Z⋆int(A))=Homk⁡(W⌀,k).H^0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(W,Z^{\mathrm{int}}_\star(A)) =\operatorname{Hom}_k(W_\varnothing,k). In particular, degree-zero maps into the singleton of this centre vanish for every differential-module source.

To see the obstruction, insert a new vacuum at pp and commute it past a coefficient at a nonempty configuration. Multiplication by (zp−zj)−1(z_p-z_j)^{-1} selects the block containing jj. On its PBW symbol, the commutator is x⟼[u−1du]⊠x,u=zp−zj,x\longmapsto[u^{-1}du]\boxtimes x,\qquad u=z_p-z_j, an injective simple-principal-part map. A central coefficient must therefore vanish on every nonempty configuration. Scalars at the empty configuration remain.

The ambient transverse endomorphism coalgebra has a different evaluation. Evaluating its unit on the vacuum recovers the nonzero local vacuum. Hence the vacuum map cannot factor through convolution-centre evaluation. In particular, there is no algebra map from the cobar of the ambient transverse endomorphism coalgebra to the convolution centre that intertwines these two specified evaluations. Both universal constructions remain valid. The obstruction concerns this direction and this evaluation condition; it does not contradict the scalar low-degree comparison.

The characteristic map

Let VV again be a degree-zero vertex algebra on 𝔸k1\mathbb A^1_k, and set 𝔤=LV\mathfrak g=L_V, C=CVC=C_V. Write ℳ(V)\mathcal M(V) for this stable category. Its vacuum is 𝔤\mathfrak g with the adjoint action.

Let ℬ\mathcal B be a differential graded vertex actor. The left differential module ℬℓ\mathcal B^\ell has connection ∂y+T\partial_y+T. This is a map of spaces from pointed actions to derived boundary-module maps. It sends paths to homotopies and a resolved action to its module roof. Its vacuum restriction is the identity. Equality of characteristic roofs does not imply that the original actions are joined by a path.

The rank-one Heisenberg vacuum gives a concrete degree-one value. At a nonzero field-valued level, C∙(Vκ)=k[x1,x2,…]⊗Λ(ξ0,ξ1,…),dxn=κnξn.C^\bullet(V_\kappa) =k[x_1,x_2,\ldots]\otimes\Lambda(\xi_0,\xi_1,\ldots), \qquad dx_n=\kappa n\xi_n. Naturality and section tests

Fix the canonical primitive-compatible tensor comparisons. These are the comparisons constructed from the factorization coefficients and their Chevalley–Cousin operations. Their envelope maps preserve the inclusion and PBW projection of primitive generators, as well as the vacuum, all partitions and collisions. Specifying only their singleton would give less data.

Theorem

In characteristic zero on the affine line, with a degree-zero boundary VV and these canonical comparisons, every pointed actor coalgebra map g:Cℬ′→Cℬg:C_{\mathcal B'}\to C_{\mathcal B} under the local vacuum induces ηg=g1ℓ⊙id𝔤⁡.\eta_g=g_1^\ell\odot\operatorname{id}_{\mathfrak g}. For every pointed action α\alpha, χ(α∘(g⊗!1C))≃χ(α)ηg.\chi\bigl(\alpha\circ(g\otimes^!1_C)\bigr) \simeq\chi(\alpha)\eta_g. The comparison preserves the full derived mapping space of differential-module section tests and is coherent for identities, compositions and parameters. The actors may be unbounded. Neither an actor augmentation to the local vacuum nor a strict vertex-algebra origin of gg or α\alpha is required.

Two contractions supply the proof. First, the envelope image of a primitive can contain higher PBW outputs. A higher output has a root carrying only ordinary vacuum inputs, whose complete positive-word complex contracts. This construction retains the pointing by using the relative source cofib⁡(Lk→Lℬ′)\operatorname{cofib}(L_k\to L_{\mathcal B'}). It concerns the canonical scalar-vacuum module action, not arbitrary boundary modules.

Second, the primitive part may differ from the module map induced by g1ℓg_1^\ell. The one-mark word complex keeps the mark at either end and in every interior position. Its residue differential contracts the kernel of singleton restriction. The regular 𝒟X\mathcal D_X probe extends this contraction to arbitrary source complexes through the unital Weyl-algebra bar resolution. At fixed word length the normal contraction is rational and bounded; the remaining perturbation raises word length, so only finitely many terms reach each output word. The existing product of mapping cochains suffices, with no completion of states or normal distributions. The same kernel contraction fills the higher composition defects.

A section test is a map of differential modules 𝒟X[−1]→ℬℓ\mathcal D_X[-1]\to\mathcal B^\ell, determined by a closed section bb and sending PP to PbPb. Its polynomial dependence on the root coordinate matters. For the free actor with odd generators cmc_m and Tcm=(m+1)cm+1Tc_m=(m+1)c_{m+1}, the map F(cm)=ycm+cm−1,c−1=0,F(c_m)=yc_m+c_{m-1},\qquad c_{-1}=0, is compatible with the full connection. After composing the positive ghost action with it, the characteristic sections are c0⟼yξ0,c1⟼ξ0,cm⟼0(m≥2).c_0\longmapsto y\xi_0,\qquad c_1\longmapsto\xi_0,\qquad c_m\longmapsto0\quad(m\geq2). Their derivative relation is ∂y(yξ0)=ξ0\partial_y(y\xi_0)=\xi_0. Taking only the fibre at y=0y=0 loses this information.

There are nonlinear actor automorphisms GpG_p with singleton identity and nonzero binary actor data, but ηGp=id⁡\eta_{G_p}=\operatorname{id}. With a suitable GG, the maps GFGF and FGFG are not pointed-homotopic, although they induce the same boundary-module map and all the displayed characteristic sections. Thus canonical naturality is compatible with nonfaithfulness of the invariant. A separate example Φ=exp⁡([b,K])\Phi=\exp([b,K]), with bb the bar differential, has a nonzero supported higher-PBW chain remainder and an explicit homotopy to the identity. A nonzero chain remainder alone is not an obstruction class.

Comparison choices have their own boundary. Start with the canonical ghost comparison ee, and replace it by e′=Cσ⊗1ee'=C_{\sigma\otimes1}e, where σ(cm)=−cm\sigma(c_m)=-c_m. Both preserve the vacuum. For the raw identity actor map, the characteristic values are now +ξ0+\xi_0 and −ξ0-\xi_0. Naturality cannot preserve the unchanged raw singleton tests at the same time. Transporting the tests by σ−1\sigma^{-1} restores the naturality map. This example is not singleton-normalized; it does not decide the comparison of independently chosen singleton-normalized tensor equivalences. That comparison requires a coherent identification of their primitive and action data with the canonical family, or an action-compatible transport of the tests.

Vacuum endomorphisms and transverse actions

For the moving Heisenberg vacuum 𝒱\mathcal V, the coefficient complex 𝔷ℓ\mathfrak z^\ell represents RHom⁡(N⊗𝒪X𝒱,𝒱)≃RHom𝒟X⁡(N,𝔷ℓ)R\operatorname{Hom}(N\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal V,\mathcal V) \simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D_X}(N,\mathfrak z^\ell) in the category of smooth modules with a moving root. A resolution obtained by adjoining two even and two odd free fields, a quartet, also constructs a coherent transverse monoid with a nontrivial ghost action and this singleton evaluation. Its singleton is universal for the displayed module problem. That monoid is not final in the full category of factorizing transverse actions. Its tower product and its separately resolved binary product agree on cohomology but are exchanged under their specified localization comparison; equality of cohomology products does not identify the operations.

Canonical naturality has a useful conditional consequence. If an admissible local centre with its specified coherent action and canonical tensor comparison exists in an action category, and finality supplies the actual map from the ghost actor, its singleton contains a degree-one section with characteristic value ξ0\xi_0. Writing that section as a finite polynomial in yy and differentiating a nonzero leading coefficient produces a constant state class with the same value. The existence of that centre, its action and the applicable finality statement remain hypotheses. The construction neither supplies them nor removes the nonfinality theorem for the full actor category.

The abelian boundary example

Pure three-dimensional 𝒩=2\mathcal N=2 U(1)U(1) gauge theory at Chern–Simons level zero has holomorphically twisted quadratic action ∫𝐁d′𝐀\int\mathbf B\,d'\mathbf A, with d′=dt∂t+dz‾∂z‾d'=dt\,\partial_t+d\bar z\,\partial_{\bar z}. There is no interaction vertex or adjoint anomaly. Neumann boundary conditions give the regular algebra Λℂ(∂znc:n≥1),Q=0,\Lambda_{\mathbb C}(\partial_z^nc:n\geq1),\qquad Q=0, with the constant ghost removed. Dirichlet boundary conditions give the perturbative regular current algebra ℂ[∂znB:n≥0],Q=0.\mathbb C[\partial_z^nB:n\geq0],\qquad Q=0. The full Dirichlet state space also requires monopole sectors. These distinctions follow from the boundary constructions of Costello, Dimofte and Gaiotto.

The two perturbative descriptions do not supply an invertible convolution bimodule or identify their module categories with all line operators. Those are additional hypotheses for applying the Morita theorem to this boundary pair. An identification with a WZW vacuum at positive effective level does not determine the full level-zero U(1)U(1) algebra.

The formal loop parameter

For a boundary at level ℏκ\hbar\kappa over ℂ[[ℏ]]\mathbb C[[\hbar]], the vacuum differential is dxn=ℏκnξndx_n=\hbar\kappa n\xi_n. The polynomial bulk complex has even generators unu_n and odd degree-one generators cmc_m, for n,m≥0n,m\geq0, with dun=κcn+1du_n=\kappa c_{n+1} and dcm=0dc_m=0. It has the map un⟼n!xn+1,cm⟼ℏm!ξm.u_n\longmapsto n!x_{n+1},\qquad c_m\longmapsto\hbar m!\xi_m. Both differentials take the first image to ℏκ(n+1)!ξn+1\hbar\kappa(n+1)!\xi_{n+1}. With completion in each cohomological degree, this is a dg algebra map and becomes an isomorphism after inverting ℏ\hbar. Before inversion, ξ1\xi_1 is nonzero in cohomology and, for κ≠0\kappa\ne0, satisfies ℏξ1=d(x1/κ).\hbar\xi_1=d(x_1/\kappa). The nonzero-level pointwise comparison therefore does not identify the entire formal parameter family. Its secondary Poisson bracket on cohomology also does not by itself construct a full little-three-disks action on the vacuum self-extensions.

An operation can vanish on state cohomology while retaining information when its insertion point moves. The Heisenberg vacuum gives an explicit example.

Theorem

At nonzero level, Kκ≃Eκ[−1]K_\kappa\simeq E_\kappa[-1], where Eκ=M⊕︎𝒪ϵ,∇E(A,a)=([∂y+T,A]−aLx1/κ,∂ya).E_\kappa=\overline M\oplus\mathcal O\epsilon,\qquad \nabla_E(\overline A,a)= \left(\overline{[\partial_y+T,A]-aL_{x_1}/\kappa},\,\partial_y a\right). Proof

The long exact cohomology sequence identifies H1(Kκ)H^1(K_\kappa) with the displayed extension and makes all other groups zero. Its connection has the stated sign because dK(x1/κ,0)=(ξ1,Lx1/κ),∇Eϵ=−Lx1/κ.d_K(x_1/\kappa,0)=(\xi_1,L_{x_1}/\kappa), \qquad \nabla_E\epsilon=-\overline{L_{x_1}/\kappa}. A horizontal splitting would give a polynomial g=A(1)g=A(1) with (∂y+T)g=x1/κ+b(y).(\partial_y+T)g=x_1/\kappa+b(y). If xNx_N is the highest state variable in gg, its left side has coefficient N∂xNgN\partial_{x_N}g at xN+1x_{N+1}. That coefficient must vanish. Repeating through the finite list leaves g∈k[y]g\in k[y], which cannot produce x1/κx_1/\kappa. Thus no horizontal splitting exists.

The zero-level fibre is different: H0(K0)=0,H1(K0)=Q01⊕︎M/L(𝒱),Hi(K0)=Q0i(i≥2).H^0(K_0)=0,\qquad H^1(K_0)=Q_0^1\oplus M/L(\mathcal V),\qquad H^i(K_0)=Q_0^i\quad(i\ge2). Its middle direct sum is split as differential modules. These are statements about the two specified field-valued levels; the parameter-dependent integral complex retains its own torsion.

The fibre also describes the ambiguity of a lift. Fix a complex NN of 𝒟\mathcal D-modules and a specified map N→MN\to M. Its lift space through QκQ_\kappa can be empty. Once a lift is chosen, this space is identified with Map𝒟⁡(N,Kκ)\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(N,K_\kappa). At nonzero level its based homotopy groups are πj=H−j−1RHom𝒟⁡(N,Eκ).\pi_j=H^{-j-1}R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(N,E_\kappa). For a free parameter N=𝒟[−s]N=\mathcal D[-s], the possible group is πs−1=Eκ\pi_{s-1}=E_\kappa. Theorem

A collision algebra AA is dualizable for ⋄\diamond precisely when its bar coalgebra BABA is perfect factorizing. This means that each coefficient, after the standard density and dimension normalization on a smooth chart, is a perfect complex over the chart’s function ring, and every coproduct component is an equivalence on its specified disjoint open. On this domain, the internal line dual is an involutive contravariant equivalence.

The coalgebra dual has pointwise dual coefficients. Its coproduct is the transpose of the inverse factorization map. Both conditions in the theorem are needed: perfect coefficients provide the finite evaluation–coevaluation pair, while inverse factorization supplies a coproduct in the required direction. The triangle identities identify the internal mapping object with this coalgebra dual.
